title: fix(security): an app-declared baseline composes with the platform `member_default` instead of replacing it (#7555)
body:
Fixes #7555

## Premise

Confirmed on `origin/main` (post-#7506). `SecurityPlugin.fallbackPermissionSet` is a **single name**: the constructor takes the explicit option, else the first `isDefault` set in the bootstrap list, else `member_default`. `appSecurityPluginOptions` funnels an app's declared `isDefault` set into that one slot, so the app's set **displaces** the platform baseline everywhere the plugin consults it — the additive step and the post-resolution fallback in `resolvePermissionSetsForContext`, `resolveFallbackPermissionSets` (ADR-0106 D7), the boot-time `everyone`-anchor binding, and the explain attribution.

Two pins in `packages/qa/dogfood` asserted the displacement in so many words: `expect(status, 'the built-in baseline is REPLACED by the declared default, not merged with it').not.toBe(200)`.

### The symptom, reproduced and fixed — measured, not reasoned

A fresh sign-up on the real booted showcase (which declares `showcase_member_default`), reading each object behind an Account-app `requiresObject` gate. Same harness, same build path, the ONLY difference being `composeHumanBaselinePermissionSets` returning `[configured]` (the pre-#7555 displacement) versus the composed list:

| object | before (displacement) | after (composition) |
|---|---|---|
| `sys_account` | **403** | **200** |
| `sys_session` | **403** | **200** |
| `sys_api_key` | **403** | **200** |
| `sys_oauth_application` | **403** | **200** |
| `sys_user_preference` | **403** | **200** |
| `sys_inbox_message` | 404 | 404 |
| `sys_notification_receipt` | 404 | 404 |

The two 404s are **not** permission verdicts — those objects are not registered on the dogfood showcase stack (no messaging service in that boot), so this harness cannot measure them either way. Reported as measured rather than folded into the win.

The issue's "23 objects vs 7" breadth figure is from an older commit and was **not** re-confirmed; the mechanism above is what was verified, and it does not depend on the counts.

## The ruling this restores

ADR-0090 **D5** (Accepted), verbatim:

> The fallback cliff is abolished. … `everyone` is additive like any other position: baseline ∪ explicit, always.

and

> `isDefault` survives with narrowed semantics: a package-authored *suggestion* consumed once at install time (D5), never a runtime fallback.

Displacement is that cliff in its second spelling: an app declaring a posture of its own silently costs its members the entire platform floor.

## The change

The human baseline becomes the **list of names** it always was — the declared set **∪** `member_default`, deduped — via a pure, unit-tested helper (`composeHumanBaselinePermissionSets`, `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/app-default-permission-set.ts`). Applied at every site that consulted the single name:

| Site | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `resolvePermissionSetsForContext` additive step | pushes one name | pushes every baseline name not already requested |
| …its post-resolution fallback | resolves `[name]` | resolves the whole list |
| `resolveFallbackPermissionSets` (ADR-0106 D7) | resolves `[name]` | resolves the whole list — see below |
| boot `everyone`-anchor binding | binds one row | binds one row per baseline name; the high-privilege refusal is now **per set** |
| `explain-engine` attribution | `name === deps.fallbackPermissionSet` | `deps.baselinePermissionSets.includes(name)` |

**D7 decision (asked for explicitly).** `resolveFallbackPermissionSets` composes too. Its whole justification is being *the same* resolution the data plane performs; one plane composing while the other displaced would put the two in disagreement about what the baseline even is, which is the drift D7 exists to prevent. On a deployment that declares no app baseline the list is exactly `['member_default']` and nothing changes; on one that does, guest schema exposure becomes platform ∪ app — both deliberate permission-set decisions, rather than an app declaration silently *narrowing* a guest's view relative to a deployment that declared nothing. Documented at the method.

### Hard edges held

- **Agent path** — `principalKind: 'agent'` still resolves `MCP_AGENT_PERMISSION_SET_RESTRICTED` and nothing else. The branch is taken **before** the composed list is consulted, so the human floor is unreachable from it (ADR-0090 D10). Pinned by its own case.
- **`fallbackPermissionSet: null`** still disables the baseline entirely — composition never re-adds one.
- **`member_default`'s grant rows** untouched (#7344's territory), and **#5491**'s narrowing of the platform baseline to explicit-allow is undisturbed: this widens nothing about the set, only *who* still resolves it.
- **D5/D9 high-privilege anchor gate** untouched.

## Consumer surfaces

`security.fallbackPermissionSet` is a registered service. Its consumers, all of them, and what each answers under composition:

| Consumer | Checked | Answer |
|---|---|---|
| `plugin-hono-server` `/auth/me/permissions` | ✅ updated | reads the new `security.baselinePermissionSets`; a member of a baseline-declaring app now gets the platform baseline's objects/fields folded into the merge instead of the app set alone |
| `plugin-hono-server` `/me/apps` (capability + tab surface) | ✅ updated | same list, so the tab/`systemPermissions` surface cannot disagree with the data plane one function call away |
| `@objectstack/verify` `harness.app-default-profile.test.ts` | ✅ checked, unchanged | reads the **declared** name, which still means exactly that — green as written |
| `packages/spec` `security-service.ts` D7 docblock | ✅ updated | prose only |

A new service `security.baselinePermissionSets: string[]` carries the composed list. `security.fallbackPermissionSet` keeps its `string | null` contract and its meaning ("the single name this deployment declared"), so no consumer breaks; the hono reads fall back to `[fallbackPermissionSet]` for a SecurityPlugin too old to register the list, and to the pre-existing bare `member_default` for a stack with no SecurityPlugin.

## Tests

New — `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/baseline-composition.test.ts` (11 cases), red in four directions: the app half, the platform half, the `null` half, the agent half. Plus a guard that the platform baseline really is the only default set granting the discriminator object, so the file cannot go quietly vacuous the way #6964 found its predecessors had.

**Reverse-verified by ablation.** Reverting `composeHumanBaselinePermissionSets` to `[configured]` turns exactly 3 of the 11 red — including the runtime case "the platform half: `member_default` is STILL in force alongside it" — while the app half, the `null` half, the agent half and the undeclared-app half stay green. That partition is the point: only the composition-bearing cases move. The same ablation, rebuilt through `dist` and re-run against the booted showcase, is the before-column of the table at the top.

One case is deliberately **not** written as a middleware `.rejects`: with zero permission sets the middleware skips its whole CRUD gate by design, so a `null`-disables case there would be red for a reason unrelated to composition and green whether or not `member_default` had been composed back in. It asserts the resolved baseline list instead, and says so.

**Semantics-flip sweep.** Both dogfood displacement pins flipped to assert the composed substance (`sys_user_preference` → 200), with the measurement tables in their headers corrected rather than deleted — the discriminator object is unchanged, only its expected direction. Refusal pins (agent exclusion, guest tier, anchor gate) stay verbatim. `showcase-d7-default-profile` also gains a new case: **both** sets are bound to the `everyone` anchor, so the explain surface reports the default a request actually applies.

Commands, real output (post-merge of `origin/main`, which now includes #7344):

```
pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-security test        → Test Files 46 passed (46) · Tests 952 passed (952)
pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-hono-server test     → Test Files 16 passed (16) · Tests 187 passed (187)
pnpm --filter @objectstack/rest test                   → Test Files 82 passed (82) · Tests 1344 passed (1344)
pnpm --filter @objectstack/verify test                 → Test Files  5 passed (5)  · Tests   23 passed (23)
pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli test                    → Test Files 109 passed (109) · Tests 1182 passed (1182)
pnpm --filter @objectstack/dogfood test (full gate)    → Test Files 87 passed | 1 skipped (88) · Tests 547 passed | 3 skipped (550)
typecheck (plugin-security, plugin-hono-server, spec)  → Done
pnpm check:docs-audit-scope                            → ✓ in sync
node scripts/check-nul-bytes.mjs                       → OK (7016 files)
```

The three baseline dogfood files, named, re-run after the #7344 merge:

```
✓ showcase-d7-default-profile > a fresh member is governed by the app-declared default (reads announcements)
✓ showcase-d7-default-profile > AND by the built-in member_default baseline — the two COMPOSE (#7555)
✓ showcase-d7-default-profile > and the explain surface tells the same story: BOTH sets are bound to the everyone anchor (#7555)
✓ showcase-default-profile    > AND by the built-in member_default baseline — the two COMPOSE (#7555)
✓ me-apps-and-everyone-baseline > bootstrap binds member_default to the everyone position (one channel, D5)
```

## Relationship to #7344 (asked for explicitly)

**#7344 LANDED mid-flight** (3987a48, "grant members owner-scoped read on the personal inbox"). It is merged into this branch and every suite above was re-run on top of it — hence 952 rather than 942 plugin-security tests.

**Does this change make #7344's fix simpler, harder, unnecessary, or unaffected? — Unaffected in code, and it is what lets #7344 REACH the users it was written for.** #7344 adds `sys_inbox_message: { allowRead: true }` plus an owner-scoped `sys_inbox_message_self` RLS policy to `member_default`. Under displacement, `member_default` does not resolve at all for a member of a baseline-declaring app — the showcase included — so that new grant would have been invisible to exactly the persona #7344's report describes. Composition is the reason the grant lands. The two fixes are complementary, and neither is sufficient alone for that persona.

**Does #7344 landing change anything here? — No.** Files are disjoint (it edits `objects/default-permission-sets.ts` grant rows; this edits the resolution), the merge was clean, and its new grants simply become part of the composed baseline automatically. One coupling worth naming: `baseline-composition.test.ts` uses `sys_user_preference` as its "granted by `member_default` and nothing else" discriminator and **asserts that property** rather than assuming it — #7344 only added grants, so the assertion holds, and if a future change broke it the guard case says so by name instead of the file going vacuous.

## Changeset

`patch` on `@objectstack/plugin-security`, `@objectstack/plugin-hono-server`, `@objectstack/spec`. Patch tier: this restores a stated ADR invariant and can only ADD grants for human principals (the evaluator merges most-permissively); no API is removed, no option changes type, and a deployment that declares no app baseline is byte-for-byte unaffected.
